subject: FootyNet, a football player recruitment platform connecting players with clubs (Next.js 15, React 19, Tailwind, en/hr i18n)
pageType: Public landing page at / for an existing multi-role web application, alongside a visual upgrade of the shared design system used by the auth screens, app shell and dashboards
scope: Continue the in-progress design work: the landing page at / is implemented with nine content sections plus navigation and footer, and the shared tokens (primary emerald-700, emerald-600 focus ring, monogram logo tile, auth side panel) are already updated. This turn advances the same brief rather than starting a new one, so the remaining work is repairing the discrepancies found in visual review against the selected references, at desktop and mobile.
primaryGoal: Raise FootyNet to professional product quality: a public landing page that explains the player-club value clearly and converts to registration, with a consistent, accessible design system carried into the app
audience: Amateur and semi-professional football players looking for clubs; club staff recruiting players; platform admins. Primarily Croatian and English speakers, on mobile and desktop.
offer: One place where players show their profile and career and apply to club job ads, and clubs post opportunities, review applicants and message them in real time
primaryAction: Register (as player or club), with Sign in as the secondary action
creativeControl: High: continue using judgment to repair reference fidelity, spacing, hierarchy and accessibility without asking, while keeping the established FootyNet identity and the already-approved section order
requiredContent: Hero: one statement of what FootyNet does, with Register and Sign in, beside a dominant media field holding the product's own interface
How it works for players: build profile, find a position, talk to the club
How it works for clubs: get approved, post a position, review applicants, message players
Product preview: an example player profile, job ad, availability and applicants view
Feature highlights: live chat, career history, availability, email alerts
Trust and process: club approval by admins, email confirmation, applications going straight to the club
Role split: separate registration actions for players and clubs
FAQ: eligibility, club approval, cost, languages, messaging, availability, mobile use
Closing call to action to register
Navigation (hero rail, compact top bar, mobile menu sheet) and footer with language choice
constraints: Keep existing Next.js App Router routes, API integration, auth flows and business logic intact
All user-facing copy stays in messages/en.json and messages/hr.json; both languages must fit without overflow
Keep Tailwind and the pitch/ink token aliases as the single place to re-theme
Respect prefers-reduced-motion; no transforms on ancestors of sticky or fixed elements
Interactive targets must be at least 44x44 CSS pixels at every reviewed viewport
No invented statistics, testimonials, real club names or partnerships; example data stays visibly labelled
No stock photography is available, so every media frame holds native HTML/CSS product interface, never a decorative SVG or fake dashboard
brandInputs: Brand accent: pitch emerald; primary fill emerald-700 #047857 with white text, hover emerald-800, focus ring emerald-600 #059669
Neutral: ink slate; canvas slate-50, white surfaces, deep pitch-green #052E22 and near-black #03140F panels
Outfit for display headings, wordmark and numbers; Inter for body and UI
FootyNet wordmark with 'Net' in the accent colour, plus a solid emerald monogram tile (the emoji was replaced)
Pitch-pattern markings used only on the hero media frame, the trust panel and the closing CTA
lucide-react is the only icon source
Existing components reused in the vignettes: Avatar, AvailabilityBadge, Badge, Button, form field styles
assumptions: 'Continue' refers to the FootyNet landing page and design-system work already in progress, not a new subject
The nine-section order (hero, players, clubs, product preview, features, trust, role split, FAQ, closing CTA) is settled and should be preserved
Visible entrance and scroll animations stay: a hero entrance on load, distinct one-time reveals for later sections, and interaction feedback, all respecting reduced motion

Example identities (NK Example, HNK Primjer, NK Uzor, Luka M., Ivan K., Marko P., Ivana K.) and the example job ads, ages, career seasons and applicant chart remain illustrative and stay visibly labelled as example data
Nav anchor links and the hero wordmark need larger hit areas to meet the 44px minimum flagged in the DOM audit
The mobile 'Build a profile like this' link is too narrow and needs a wider or full-width target
unresolved: Whether pricing exists for clubs or players (the FAQ states only that registration asks for no payment details)
Whether a dark mode is wanted for the app (not planned)
